subject: general
question: Proteins are mainly responsible for which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Growth and repair of tissues**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proteins** are essential macromolecules required for the **growth, repair, and maintenance of body tissues**. They play a crucial role in cell regeneration and healing wounds.
 
• Proteins are made up of **amino acids**, which are the building blocks necessary for the formation of muscles, skin, and internal organs.
 
• Unlike carbohydrates, proteins are primarily responsible for **structural and functional roles** in the body rather than being a quick energy source.
 
• Proteins also contribute to the production of **enzymes, hormones, and antibodies**, all of which are vital for maintaining body functions and immunity.
 
• In the absence of adequate protein intake, individuals may suffer from conditions like **muscle wasting**, weakened immune response, and delayed wound healing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of Proteins:**

 
 
• **Structural Function:** Proteins like collagen and keratin provide strength and support to tissues such as skin, hair, and nails.
 
• **Enzymatic Function:** Enzymes are proteins that catalyze biochemical reactions in the body, aiding in digestion, metabolism, and other vital processes.
 
• **Transport Function:** Proteins such as hemoglobin transport oxygen in the blood, while others assist in moving nutrients across cell membranes.
 
• **Immune Function:** Antibodies, composed of proteins, are crucial for fighting infections and ensuring immunity.
 
• **Hormonal Function:** Some hormones like insulin are protein-based and regulate various body functions, including blood sugar levels.
 
 
 
• **Sources of Proteins:**
 
 
• **Animal Sources:** Eggs, milk, meat, fish, and poultry are rich in high-quality proteins containing all essential amino acids.
 
• **Plant Sources:** Legumes, beans, nuts, seeds, and soy products provide protein for vegetarians and vegans.
 
• **Dairy Products:** Cheese, yogurt, and whey are excellent sources of proteins, especially for muscle repair.
 
 
 
• **Protein Deficiency:**
 
 
• Protein deficiency can lead to conditions such as **kwashiorkor**, characterized by swelling, fatigue, and poor growth.
 
• Individuals with inadequate protein intake may experience **weakened immune systems** and increased susceptibility to infections.
 
 
 
• **Quick Energy Sources:**
 
 
• **Carbohydrates:** These are the primary source of quick energy for the body, stored as glycogen and metabolized for immediate energy.
 
• Proteins are not typically used as a primary energy source unless the body is in a state of starvation or prolonged physical exertion.
 
 
 
• **Improving Digestion:**
 
 
• Proteins such as digestive enzymes (e.g., pepsin, trypsin) play a role in breaking down food into absorbable nutrients.
 
• However, proteins themselves are not directly responsible for enhancing digestion as a primary function.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Daily Protein Requirements:**

 
 
• The recommended daily protein intake varies based on **age, gender, and physical activity**. For an average adult, it is approximately **0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight**.
 
• Athletes and bodybuilders may require higher amounts to support muscle growth and repair.
 
 
 
• **Protein Quality:**
 
 
• Proteins are classified based on their amino acid content. **Complete proteins** (e.g., from animal sources) contain all essential amino acids.
 
• **Incomplete proteins** (e.g., from plant sources) may lack one or more essential amino acids but can be complemented by combining different food sources.
 
 
 
• **Proteins vs. Other Nutrients:**
 
 
• **Carbohydrates:** Primarily provide energy through glucose metabolism.
 
• **Fats:** Serve as long-term energy storage and support cell structure and hormone production.
 
• **Proteins:** Focus on structural, enzymatic, and functional roles rather than immediate energy provision.
